title: Workspaces incorrectly moves main chrome window instead of PWA app
summary: This Workspaces report was filed on 0.99.1, and current merged PWA-recognition work appears to cover the “plain Chrome window moved instead of PWA” failure mode.
next_action: Draft a comment pointing to the newer Workspaces PWA matching fixes and ask for a retest on a current build if the symptom remains.

confidence.rationale: The current code and merged history explicitly strengthen Chrome/Edge PWA identification, but the artifact should still present this as likely-covered rather than absolutely proven.

judgment.rationale: Current Workspaces PWA-recognition changes appear to address the window-matching ambiguity described in this older-build report.
evidence: The issue was filed against PowerToys 0.99.1 and describes a normal Chrome window being moved as if it were a saved PWA entry.
Current Workspaces matching logic in WindowArranger.cpp compares both app identity and pwaAppId before reusing an existing window.
Merged follow-up PRs #36217 and #39971 both focused specifically on PWA recognition and PWA launch handling.
judgment.recommended_action: Point the reporter to the newer Workspaces PWA fixes and ask for a retest on a current build before starting a fresh design.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current merged PWA follow-up and launch work appears to cover the PWA-identification path reported here.

issue_context.summary: The report says Workspaces confused a saved Chrome-hosted PWA with a normal Chrome window and moved the wrong window during workspace activation.
known_information: The issue is on PowerToys 0.99.1, much older than the current main branch.
The saved workspace contains Google Chat, Calendar, and Gmail PWA windows hosted in Chrome.
When the workspace is activated, a plain Chrome window on the target monitor is moved and the remaining PWA opens on top of it.
inferences: The bug is in Workspaces window matching rather than in monitor positioning alone, because the wrong already-open Chrome-hosted window is reused.
Later PWA follow-up work likely covered this by using explicit PWA identity rather than plain chrome.exe path matching.
issue_context.analysis: The issue looks like an older-build instance of Workspaces’ PWA identity ambiguity. Current code and PR history show targeted work in exactly that area, so the right correction is to treat it as likely-covered existing work first.
initial_investigation: WindowArranger.cpp now extracts Chrome/Edge PWA identity and requires pwaAppId equality when matching an already-open window to a saved workspace entry.
WorkspacesLib/PwaHelper.cpp contains explicit Chrome and Edge PWA app-ID extraction logic.
PR #36217 and PR #39971 are both directly about Workspaces PWA follow-up and launch correctness.

actions.label: Point to Workspaces PWA matching fixes

comment.body: This looks likely covered by the newer Workspaces PWA work in PR #36217 and PR #39971. Current Workspaces matching logic now carries explicit PWA identity instead of treating every Chrome-hosted window as the same generic chrome.exe target. Because this report was filed on 0.99.1, I would first ask for a retest on a current build before opening a new design track; if a plain Chrome window is still reused instead of the saved PWA, the next useful artifact would be a fresh workspace export from the newer build.
